title: PETRI: Learning Unified Cell Embeddings from Unpaired Modalities via Early-Fusion Joint Reconstruction
abstract: Integrating multimodal screening data is challenging because biological signals only partially overlap and cell-level pairing is frequently unavailable. Existing approaches either require pairing or fail to capture both shared and modality-specific information in an end-to-end manner. We present PETRI, an early-fusion transformer that learns a unified cell embedding from unpaired cellular images and gene expression profiles. PETRI groups cells by shared experimental context into multimodal “documents” and performs masked joint reconstruction with cross-modal attention, permitting information sharing while preserving modality-specific capacity. The resulting latent space supports construction of perturbation-level profiles by simple averaging across modalities. Applying sparse autoencoders to the embeddings reveals learned concepts that are biologically meaningful, multimodal, and retain perturbation-specific effects. To support further machine learning research, we release a blinded, matched optical pooled screen (OPS) and Perturb-seq dataset in HepG2 cells.
problem: Integrating multimodal biological screening data is difficult because signals partially overlap and cell-level pairing is frequently unavailable.
approach: PETRI is an early-fusion transformer learning unified cell embeddings via masked joint reconstruction of unpaired cellular images and gene expression, with cross-modal attention enabling information sharing.
contribution: Supports perturbation-level profiles via simple averaging and sparse autoencoder analysis reveals learned concepts that are biologically meaningful and preserve perturbation effects.
